title: Republic of Ireland’s Sammie Szmodics knocked unconscious in World Cup playoff
content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics was taken off on a stretcher after being knocked unconscious during Thursday’s World Cup playoff against the Czech Republic.

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson confirmed at full time Szmodics had regained consciousness and would remain in Prague overnight.

Szmodics, 30, fell to the floor after challenging for an aerial ball in the second half of extra time. He received treatment on the pitch for several minutes before being taken off on a stretcher and was applauded off by the crowd at the Fortuna Arena in Prague.

“He was knocked out cold,” Hallgrimsson told broadcaster RTE at full time. “At least he’s conscious now. He will stay here tonight and will hopefully fly home tomorrow.”

The forward had been introduced as a substitute in the 115th minute of Thursday’s fixture, before suffering the collision minutes later.

He was replaced by Harvey Vale in the 121st minute, who was making his senior Ireland debut.

Thursday’s game finished in a 2-2 draw after the Czech Republic came from two goals down to force extra time.

The hosts subsequently advanced to a playoff final against Denmark after winning 4-3 on penalties.

Szmodics is on loan at Derby County from Ipswich Town and has scored three times in 26 appearances in all competitions this season.
